vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: intelligence-suite
Version: 1.0.2

The OpenClaw skill 'intelligence-suite' is designed for web scraping news and AI-related content. All network requests in `scripts/monitor.js` and `scripts/scan.js` are directed to domains explicitly listed in the `SKILL.md` permissions (e.g., reuters.com, scmp.com, openai.com, firebaseio.com). The scripts use standard libraries (axios, cheerio, rss-parser) for fetching and parsing content, and output results to stdout for the agent. There is no evidence of data exfiltration to unauthorized endpoints, arbitrary command execution, obfuscation, or malicious prompt injection attempts within `SKILL.md`. The requested `filesystem: [read]` permission is broad but not exploited in a suspicious manner by the provided code.

llm.summary: The skill mostly does what it says (RSS fetching + scraping) and uses expected Node libraries, but there is a mismatch between declared network permissions and the script's behavior (it will follow links from feeds, including arbitrary HN-linked URLs), which is a notable incoherence you should understand before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the code: the scripts fetch RSS feeds, deep-scrape articles, and produce structured output for an agent. Declared required binaries (node, npm) and npm deps (axios, cheerio, rss-parser) are appropriate for the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and scripts say they perform 'deep scrape' of article URLs. scan.js obtains URLs from Hacker News items (s.url) and then fetches those links directly — those target domains can be arbitrary. SKILL.md's listed network permissions enumerate a limited set of domains, but the runtime instructions and code will attempt requests to feed-supplied links that may be outside that list (e.g., personal blogs, arXiv, theverge.com). That mismatch means the skill may attempt network access beyond the declared scope.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No remote binary download or extract; standard npm install of common packages is required. This is a normal install pattern for Node scripts, but npm installs pull third-party packages from the registry (moderate trust surface).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or credentials. The behavior (fetching public feeds and scraping) does not require secrets, so the lack of credential requests is proportionate.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true, does not claim to modify other skills, and does not write persistent system-wide config. It only logs to stdout for the agent to consume.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill uses node + npm and installs common scraping libraries; that part is normal for a news-scraper. The main risk is network scope: although SKILL.md lists a small set of allowed domains, the scripts will follow feed-supplied links (especially from Hacker News), which can point to arbitrary hosts. Before installing, consider: (1) whether your platform enforces the declared network allowlist (if it does, unexpected external fetches will be blocked); (2) whether you are comfortable the agent will fetch and locally process HTML from arbitrary external sites; (3) running npm install and the scripts in a sandboxed environment first; (4) reviewing/locking the feed list if you only want specific domains; and (5) auditing dependencies (axios, cheerio, rss-parser) to ensure no supply-chain concerns. If you need a lower blast radius, ask the author to constrain the code to only fetch from explicitly whitelisted hosts or remove the Hacker News external-link behavior.
